name: kaggle_competition_skills
description: Kaggle competition skills extracted from 20+ real competitions (6 Gold medals). Contains validated strategies for tabular, time series, CV, NLP, RL, ONNX, and simulation competitions. Includes dead-end avoidance (30+ confirmed failure patterns) and cross-domain transfer rules. Use when participating in ML competitions or benchmark tasks.
prompt_template: Always run AutoGluon as the FIRST baseline before manual feature engineering (autogluon-first).
Use ONE variable per experiment — never bundle multiple changes (controlled-variable principle).
Always compare OOF score against LB score. Small data (N<1000) can have 0.03-0.09 OOF/LB gap. If OOF improves but LB doesn't, you are overfitting the CV.
When model correlation > 0.93, ensembling yields < 0.001 improvement. Only add low-correlation models to break through stacking ceilings.
For time series: use TimeSeriesPredictor (not TabularPredictor). Chronos-2 supports known_covariates natively. If HF_ENDPOINT causes download errors, pre-download models and pass local paths.
Check submission format BEFORE submitting (id column names, probability vs hard labels, negative values). 12 wasted submissions from format errors across competitions.
For simulation competitions (TrueSkill): re-submitting resets convergence. Latest-N rule means only most recent submissions count.
For code competitions: fork public baselines (80% of work). Add artifact datasets as kernel inputs.
After each experiment: extract skill or record dead-end. Knowledge crystallization is mandatory.
